## About This Framework

The **IaCM Well-Architected Framework** defines six foundational pillars for designing, operating, and governing Infrastructure as Code at enterprise scale. It draws from real-world adoption patterns observed across production Harness IaCM deployments, HashiCorp Terraform best practices, DORA research on software delivery performance, NIST CSF for cloud security, and FinOps Foundation principles.

Each pillar contains design principles, implementation guidance, maturity indicators, and anti-patterns to avoid. Use the self-assessment at the end of each pillar to score your current state and identify where to focus improvement.

::: metrics
- label: Pillars
  value: "6"
  sub: covering the full IaCM lifecycle
- label: Design Principles
  value: "36"
  sub: six per pillar
- label: Best Practices

  sub: derived from live pipeline analysis
:::

:::info
**How to use this framework:** Read each pillar, run the self-assessment, and score your current state (1–5). Use the gap analysis to build a prioritised backlog. Revisit quarterly as your IaCM adoption matures.
:::

## The Six Pillars

| # | Pillar | Core Question |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pipeline Design & Lifecycle** | Are your IaC pipelines consistent, composable, and complete? |
| 2 | **Security & Compliance** | Is every infrastructure change scanned, governed, and audited? |
| 3 | **State Management & Reliability** | Is your Terraform state protected, versioned, and recoverable? |
| 4 | **Workspace Governance** | Are workspaces well-structured, named, and access-controlled? |
| 5 | **Cost & FinOps Integration** | Do engineers see the cost impact of changes before they apply them? |
| 6 | **Developer Experience & Enablement** | Can teams self-serve IaCM without needing platform expertise? |

## Pillar 1: Pipeline Design & Lifecycle

> *"A well-designed IaCM pipeline is the single source of truth for how infrastructure changes flow from code to cloud."*

### Design Principles

1. **Every lifecycle action has a pipeline.** Plan, apply, destroy, and drift detection are all first-class pipeline citizens — not ad-hoc console operations.
2. **Pipelines are declarative, not imperative.** Pipeline YAML lives in version control alongside Terraform code. Changes to pipelines go through the same review process as infrastructure changes.
3. **One canonical pipeline pattern per environment tier.** Dev, staging, and production use the same pipeline template with environment-scoped variable overrides — not separate pipeline YAMLs.
4. **Conditional execution over multiple pipelines.** Use stage variables (`TF_Action: apply|destroy|dry-run`) to control execution paths rather than maintaining separate apply and destroy pipelines.
5. **Templates at the highest practical scope.** Security scans, approval gates, and notification steps belong in account- or org-level templates, not duplicated per project.
6. **Pipelines are observable.** Every run emits structured logs, cost delta, scan results, and drift status to a centralised dashboard.

### The IaCM Pipeline Lifecycle

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        IACM PIPELINE LIFECYCLE                               │
├──────────┬──────────┬───────────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────┬───────────┤
│  CLONE   │   INIT   │   PLAN    │   SCAN   │  GATE    │  ACT    │  VERIFY   │
│          │          │           │          │          │         │           │
│ GitClone │ tf init  │ tf plan   │ Security │ Approval │ apply   │ drift     │
│ or Code  │ backend  │ + plan    │ + Cost   │ + OPA    │   or    │ detect +  │
│ trigger  │ config   │ JSON out  │ + Policy │ + Budget │ destroy │ outputs   │
└──────────┴──────────┴───────────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────────┴───────────┘
     ▲                                                                 │
     └─────────────── GitOps trigger (PR merge / push to main) ───────┘
```

### Pipeline Patterns

#### Pattern 1 — Unified Lifecycle Pipeline (Recommended)

A single pipeline controls all lifecycle actions via a `TF_Action` stage variable. Observed in production at AISADMINIAC (TU Africa). Best for teams that want minimal pipeline sprawl.

| Strengths | When to Use |
|---|---|
| Single pipeline per workspace | Teams managing many workspaces |
| Conditional step execution | When plan/apply/destroy share common steps |
| Unified audit trail | Compliance-driven environments |

#### Pattern 2 — Dedicated Per-Action Pipelines

Separate pipelines for plan, apply, destroy, drift. Backed by a shared org-level template. Observed in production at TU UK. Best for teams using pipeline-as-code Git triggers.

| Strengths | When to Use |
|---|---|
| Clean separation of concerns | PR-driven GitOps workflows |
| Easy to trigger individually | Webhook / CI integration |
| Simpler pipeline YAML | Teams new to IaCM |

#### Pattern 3 — Orchestrated Multi-Stage Pipeline

Pre-setup stage (secrets/credentials), workspace management stage, then IaCM execution. Observed in production at OneTru/Vanguard (GCP). Best for complex multi-environment deployments.

| Strengths | When to Use |
|---|---|
| Full environment lifecycle | Dynamic workspace provisioning |
| Vault / secrets orchestration | Zero-trust credential models |
| Multi-region deployments | Platform engineering teams |

### Step Type Reference

| Step | Type | Purpose | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Init | `IACMTerraformPlugin: init` | Backend init, provider download | Always |
| Plan | `IACMTerraformPlugin: plan` | Dry-run, outputs plan JSON | Always |
| Apply | `IACMTerraformPlugin: apply` | Provision infrastructure | Conditional |
| Destroy | `IACMTerraformPlugin: destroy` | Teardown infrastructure | Conditional |
| Detect Drift | `IACMTerraformPlugin: detect-drift` | Compare state vs reality | Recommended |
| Approval | `IACMApproval` | Human gate with plan diff UI | Always (apply/destroy) |
| Security Scan | Step Group (template ref) | Wiz / Checkov / STO | Always |
| Cost Estimation | Plugin (Infracost) | Cost delta pre-apply | Recommended |
| OPA Policy | `Policy` step | Compliance enforcement | Recommended |
| Outputs Export | `Run` step | Pass infra outputs to CD | When consumed downstream |

### Anti-Patterns

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: Running `terraform apply` manually from a developer laptop.** Every infrastructure change must flow through a pipeline. Manual applies break the audit trail, bypass security scans, and cause state drift. Enforce this via RBAC — only the pipeline service account should have cloud write permissions.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: One pipeline per resource.** A pipeline for each S3 bucket, RDS instance, and security group creates unmanageable sprawl. Group related resources into workspaces managed by a single pipeline.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Hardcoding environment differences.** Separate `pipeline_dev.yaml` and `pipeline_prod.yaml` files diverge over time. Use stage variables and template inputs with environment-scoped overrides instead.
:::

### Self-Assessment — Pillar 1

| Capability | Level 1 | Level 3 | Level 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline coverage | Some resources have pipelines | All apply operations use pipelines | All lifecycle actions (plan/apply/destroy/drift) have pipelines |
| Template usage | No templates | Project-level templates | Org/account-level templates for all security and governance steps |
| Pipeline-as-code | Pipelines created in UI | Pipelines in YAML | Pipelines in Git with PR review |
| Conditional execution | Separate apply/destroy pipelines | Stage variables control execution | Dynamic execution based on policy and cost outcomes |

## Pillar 2: Security & Compliance

> *"Infrastructure code is code. Every change deserves the same security scrutiny as application code — ideally more, since it defines the attack surface."*

### Design Principles

1. **Shift security left.** Scan IaC at plan time — before any resource is created. Post-apply scanning is too late.
2. **Centralise scanning in templates.** Security tools belong in account-level templates, not copy-pasted into each pipeline. One template update covers all pipelines.
3. **Gate on findings, don't just report them.** CRITICAL and HIGH findings should block the pipeline. Warning-only scans are not security controls — they are security theatre.
4. **Defence in depth.** Use multiple complementary tools: static analysis (Wiz/Checkov), secrets detection (tfsec/Trivy), policy enforcement (OPA), and runtime monitoring (Harness STO).
5. **Treat secrets as first-class citizens.** No credentials in HCL, no credentials in pipeline YAML, no credentials in variable defaults. Use dynamic credential providers (OIDC, Vault AppRole).
6. **Audit everything.** Every pipeline run, approval decision, policy override, and plan output is an audit event. Retain for compliance.

### The Security Scanning Stack

::: metrics
- label: Layer 1
  value: "IaC Static"
  sub: Wiz IaC / Checkov
- label: Layer 2
  value: "Secrets"
  sub: tfsec / Trivy / Gitleaks
- label: Layer 3
  value: "Policy"
  sub: OPA / Conftest
- label: Layer 4
  value: "Runtime"
  sub: Harness STO
- label: Layer 5
  value: "Compliance"
  sub: CIS / PCI / HIPAA
- label: Layer 6
  value: "Supply Chain"
  sub: SBOM / module signing
:::

### Tool Selection Guide

| Tool | Category | What It Catches | Integration Point | OSS / Commercial |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Wiz IaC** | Static analysis | Cloud misconfigs, CIS benchmarks, NIST | Post-plan step group | Commercial |
| **Checkov** | Static analysis | HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC2 compliance policies | Post-plan Plugin step | OSS |
| **tfsec** | Secrets + misconfig | Hardcoded credentials, open security groups | Pre-plan or post-plan | OSS |
| **Trivy** | Secrets + SBOM | Credentials, provider vulnerabilities, SBOM | Post-plan | OSS |
| **OPA / Conftest** | Policy as code | Business rules, tagging, naming, approved regions | Post-plan Policy step | OSS |
| **Harness STO** | Orchestration | Aggregates all tools, pass/fail gates, dashboard | Dedicated STO stage | Commercial |
| **Infracost** | Cost policy | Budget threshold violations | Post-plan Plugin step | OSS + Commercial |
| **Gitleaks** | Secrets in Git | Credentials committed to IaC repos | Pre-clone or CI step | OSS |

### Scanning Pipeline Position

```
init → plan → [SCAN ZONE] → approval → apply

SCAN ZONE contains (in order):
  1. Secrets detection (tfsec / Gitleaks)       ← fastest, fail fast
  2. IaC static analysis (Wiz IaC / Checkov)   ← misconfigs
  3. Policy enforcement (OPA / Conftest)         ← business rules
  4. Cost estimation (Infracost)                 ← budget gate
  5. Compliance report generation               ← audit artefact
```

### Severity Gates

| Severity | Wiz/Checkov | OPA | Cost Delta | Recommended Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CRITICAL | Block | Block | > $50k/month | Block — override requires CISO approval |
| HIGH | Block | Block | > $10k/month | Block — override requires manager + comment |
| MEDIUM | Warn | Warn | > $5k/month | Warn — approval note required |
| LOW | Info | Info | > $1k/month | Inform — no gate |
| Informational | Info | — | < $1k/month | Log only |

### Secrets Management Architecture

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │   Harness Secrets Store  │
                    │  (encrypted at rest,     │
                    │   project/org scoped)    │
                    └──────────┬──────────────┘
                               │ <+secrets.getValue("...")>
             ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐
             ▼                 ▼                 ▼
    ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
    │  Vault       │  │  OIDC / WIF  │  │  Cloud       │
    │  AppRole     │  │  (AWS / GCP  │  │  Connector   │
    │  (Dynamic    │  │  / Azure)    │  │  (Harness    │
    │  credentials)│  │  No keys     │  │  managed)    │
    └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
         ▲                  ▲                  ▲
         │                  │                  │
    HashiCorp         Cloud IAM             Short-lived
    Vault cluster     role trust            tokens only
```

**Credential hierarchy (most to least preferred):**

1. **OIDC / Workload Identity** — No stored credentials at all. Cloud IAM trusts the Harness pipeline identity directly.
2. **Vault AppRole** — Dynamic short-lived credentials from HashiCorp Vault. Observed in Vanguard/OneTru production deployment.
3. **Harness Cloud Connector** — Credentials stored encrypted in Harness, rotated via secret manager integration.
4. **Harness Secret** — Static credential in Harness secrets store. Acceptable with mandatory rotation policy.
5. **Pipeline variable / hardcoded** — **Never acceptable in production.**

### OPA Policy Examples

**Mandatory tagging policy:**
```rego
package terraform.tags

required_tags := {"Environment", "Team", "Owner", "CostCentre"}

deny[msg] {
  resource := input.resource_changes[_]
  resource.change.after != null
  missing := required_tags - {tag | resource.change.after.tags[tag]}
  count(missing) > 0
  msg := sprintf("'%v' is missing required tags: %v",
                 [resource.address, missing])
}
```

**Approved regions policy:**
```rego
package terraform.regions

approved := {"us-east-1", "us-west-2", "eu-west-1", "ap-southeast-1"}

deny[msg] {
  resource := input.resource_changes[_]
  region := resource.change.after.region
  not approved[region]
  msg := sprintf("'%v' targets unapproved region '%v'", [resource.address, region])
}
```

**No public S3 buckets:**
```rego
package terraform.s3

deny[msg] {
  resource := input.resource_changes[_]
  resource.type == "aws_s3_bucket_acl"
  resource.change.after.acl == "public-read"
  msg := sprintf("S3 bucket '%v' must not be public", [resource.address])
}
```

### Anti-Patterns

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: Scanning after apply.** If a misconfiguration is found post-apply, you now have a non-compliant resource in production and a remediation pipeline run to execute. Always scan the plan, block on findings, never let bad config reach the cloud.
:::

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: Secrets in `.tfvars` files committed to Git.** Even in private repos. Use `.gitignore` for all `.tfvars` files containing sensitive data. Use Harness secrets or Vault for all credential values.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Scan-but-never-block.** Running Checkov or Wiz as informational steps that never fail the pipeline provides false confidence. Define and enforce severity gates from day one.
:::

### Self-Assessment — Pillar 2

| Capability | Level 1 | Level 3 | Level 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| IaC scanning | No scanning | Single tool (Wiz or Checkov) | Multi-layer (static + secrets + policy + cost) |
| Scan gates | Warnings only | Block on CRITICAL | Block on HIGH, warn on MEDIUM, STO dashboard |
| Secrets management | Variables / hardcoded | Harness Secrets | OIDC / Vault AppRole (no stored credentials) |
| Policy as code | No policies | Manual tagging enforcement | OPA policies in Git, evaluated on every plan |
| Audit trail | Pipeline logs only | Structured scan results | Centralised compliance dashboard with retention |

## Pillar 3: State Management & Reliability

> *"Terraform state is the ground truth of your infrastructure. Treat it with the same care as a production database."*

### Design Principles

1. **Remote state only.** Local state files are a single point of failure and cannot be shared across teams or pipeline runs.
2. **State locking is non-negotiable.** Two simultaneous applies against the same workspace will corrupt state. Use a backend that supports locking (S3+DynamoDB, GCS, Azure Blob, or Harness IaCM managed state).
3. **State is versioned and recoverable.** Enable versioning on your state backend. Know your recovery procedure before you need it.
4. **Workspaces isolate blast radius.** One workspace per environment tier per application component. Never share state across unrelated resources.
5. **State migration is a first-class pipeline operation.** Moving resources between workspaces or backends is done via a dedicated pipeline — not manual CLI commands.
6. **Never edit state manually.** `terraform state rm`, `terraform state mv`, and `terraform import` run through pipelines with approval gates, not ad-hoc from developer terminals.

### State Backend Comparison

| Backend | Locking | Versioning | Encryption | Harness IaCM Native | Recommended For |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Harness IaCM Managed** | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Yes | All new projects |
| AWS S3 + DynamoDB | ✅ DynamoDB | ✅ S3 versioning | ✅ SSE-KMS | ✅ Via connector | AWS-native teams |
| GCS | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Object versioning | ✅ CMEK | ✅ Via connector | GCP-native teams |
| Azure Blob | ✅ Lease-based | ✅ Blob versioning | ✅ CMK | ✅ Via connector | Azure-native teams |
| Terraform Cloud | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ✅ Built-in | ⚠️ Migration needed | HashiCorp Cloud |
| Local | ❌ None | ❌ None | ❌ None | ❌ No | **Never in production** |

### Workspace Isolation Model

```
Application: PaymentService
│
├── workspace: payment_service_networking_dev
├── workspace: payment_service_networking_stg
├── workspace: payment_service_networking_prod
│
├── workspace: payment_service_compute_dev
├── workspace: payment_service_compute_stg
├── workspace: payment_service_compute_prod
│
└── workspace: payment_service_database_dev
    workspace: payment_service_database_stg
    workspace: payment_service_database_prod

Rule: One state file per (component × environment). Never share state.
```

### Disaster Recovery Runbook

| Scenario | Detection | Recovery Procedure | RTO |
|---|---|---|---|
| State file corruption | Plan fails with state errors | Restore from last versioned backup, re-run plan to verify | < 1 hour |
| State lock stuck | Timeout on pipeline run | Check lock holder, manually force-unlock via pipeline (not CLI) | < 30 min |
| Workspace deleted accidentally | Pipeline 404 on workspace API | Re-create workspace, import state from backup, re-run drift detect | 2–4 hours |
| Backend unreachable | Init fails | Failover to backup backend (S3 → secondary region), update backend config | < 2 hours |
| Partial apply failure | Apply exits non-zero mid-run | Do NOT re-run blindly — run plan first, inspect diff, apply with targeted changes | 1–2 hours |

### State Migration Pipeline (Real Pattern from AISADMINIAC)

:::success
**Production pattern observed:** TU Africa's AISADMINIAC project uses a dedicated `saiac-statefile-migration-dev` pipeline for Terraform state migrations. This is the correct approach — state operations go through the same pipeline governance as infrastructure changes.
:::

```yaml
# State migration pipeline pattern
stages:
  - stage:
      type: IACM
      execution:
        steps:
          - step:
              type: IACMTerraformPlugin
              name: init_source
              spec:
                command: init
                # Source backend config
          - step:
              type: IACMApproval      # Always gate state operations
              name: State_Migration_Approval
              spec:
                autoApprove: false
              timeout: 4h
          - step:
              type: Run
              name: migrate_state
              spec:
                command: |
                  terraform state mv \
                    -state=old.tfstate \
                    -state-out=new.tfstate \
                    "${SOURCE_RESOURCE}" "${DEST_RESOURCE}"
          - step:
              type: IACMTerraformPlugin
              name: validate_new_state
              spec:
                command: plan  # Should show no changes
```

### CloudFormation to Terraform Migration

:::info
**Real pattern observed:** TU Africa runs an active `Cloudformation_to_Terraform` migration pipeline using the `CTT_Terraform_Migration` template. The pattern uses `terraform import` to bring existing AWS resources under Terraform management, followed by Wiz scanning and drift detection to verify fidelity.
:::

**Migration pipeline flow:**
1. `terraform init` — initialise new Terraform workspace
2. `terraform import` — import existing CloudFormation resource into state
3. **Wiz IaC scan** — verify imported resource config is compliant
4. `terraform plan` — should show zero diff if import was clean
5. Approval gate — human verification before commit
6. `detect-drift` — confirm live resource matches new Terraform state

### Anti-Patterns

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: Shared state across environments.** Using the same `terraform.tfstate` for dev and production means a failed dev apply can corrupt production state. Always use separate workspaces per environment.
:::

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: Manual `terraform state` commands from a developer machine.** State manipulation bypasses the pipeline audit trail, has no approval gate, and cannot be reviewed or rolled back. All state operations must run through IaCM pipelines.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: No state backup.** If your state backend doesn't have versioning enabled and your state file is corrupted or deleted, you have no record of what resources Terraform manages. Enable versioning on day one.
:::

### Self-Assessment — Pillar 3

| Capability | Level 1 | Level 3 | Level 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| State backend | Local files | Remote backend (S3/GCS/Azure) | Harness IaCM managed state with locking |
| State isolation | Monolithic state | Per-application state | Per-component per-environment workspace isolation |
| State recovery | No backup | Manual backup | Versioned backend + tested recovery runbook |
| State operations | Manual CLI | CLI with documentation | All state operations via IaCM pipelines with approval |
| Drift handling | Unknown | Manual detection | Automated drift pipelines with alerting and remediation |

## Pillar 4: Workspace Governance

> *"A workspace is the unit of ownership in IaCM. Good workspace design maps directly to team structure, environment topology, and cost allocation."*

### Design Principles

1. **Workspaces follow team topology.** One team owns one or more workspaces. No workspace is owned by multiple teams (Conway's Law applies to infrastructure too).
2. **Naming conventions are enforced, not suggested.** Workspace names encode environment, region, application, and component. This makes cost attribution, RBAC, and drift detection deterministic.
3. **RBAC is workspace-scoped.** Developers can plan against all workspaces they own, but can only apply to non-production. Production applies require elevated access tied to the pipeline service account.
4. **Workspaces are provisioned by pipelines.** The creation, modification, and deletion of workspaces is itself an IaCM operation — not a manual UI click.
5. **Every workspace has an owner tag.** Team, CostCentre, Environment, Application, and Region are mandatory workspace tags. Untagged workspaces are automatically flagged.
6. **Workspace lifecycle is managed.** Workspaces have a creation date, a review cadence, and a decommission process. Abandoned workspaces are a cost and security risk.

### Workspace Naming Convention

```
{org}-{team}-{application}-{component}-{environment}-{region}

Examples:
  tuk-platform-payments-networking-prod-use1
  tuaf-aisadmin-aurora-rds-dev-use1
  onetru-vanguard-gke-cluster-nonprod-usc1
  intl-attributes-vm-web-test-euw1

Field     Length  Values
────────────────────────────────────────────────────
org       3-6     tuk, tuaf, onetru, intl, gloinfra
team      2-12    platform, aisadmin, vanguard
app       2-16    payments, aurora, gke
component 2-12    networking, rds, cluster, s3
env       3-5     dev, stg, prod, test, dr
region    4-5     use1, usw2, euw1, apse1, usc1
```

### RBAC Model

| Role | Plan | Apply (Non-Prod) | Apply (Prod) | Destroy | State Ops | Workspace Admin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Developer** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Team Lead** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (approval) | ✅ (approval) | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Platform Engineer** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (pipeline) | ✅ |
| **Pipeline Service Account** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| **Read-Only / Auditor** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

### Workspace Lifecycle

```
         ┌──────────────┐
         │   Request    │  ← Self-service catalog form
         │  (Jira/ITSM) │
         └──────┬───────┘
                ▼
         ┌──────────────┐
         │  Provision   │  ← IaCM pipeline creates workspace
         │  Pipeline    │    assigns RBAC, sets tags
         └──────┬───────┘
                ▼
         ┌──────────────┐
         │   Active     │  ← Regular applies, drift detection
         │  Operations  │    cost monitoring
         └──────┬───────┘
                ▼ (quarterly review)
         ┌──────────────┐
         │   Review     │  ← Cost > threshold? Resources still needed?
         │              │    Reassign owner if team changes
         └──────┬───────┘
                ▼ (decommission request)
         ┌──────────────┐
         │  Destroy +   │  ← IaCM destroy pipeline
         │  Archive     │    state archived, workspace closed
         └──────────────┘
```

### Workspace Provisioning via IaCM (OneTru / Vanguard Pattern)

:::success
**Production pattern observed:** The Vanguard GKE cluster pipeline uses a `Manage_IACM_Workspace` template (v1.0.5) to dynamically create and configure workspaces as part of the pipeline itself. Workspace names are derived from environment variables (`<+pipeline.variables.environment>_gke_cluster`), ensuring naming consistency programmatically.
:::

This is the gold standard — workspaces are not manually created in the UI. They are provisioned by a pipeline, with their name, tags, Git connector, and Terraform version all set programmatically.

### Anti-Patterns

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Monolithic workspaces.** Putting all infrastructure for an application (networking, compute, database, DNS) into a single workspace creates a massive blast radius. One failed resource change locks the entire workspace while it's in a bad state.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Shared workspaces across teams.** When two teams share a workspace, neither owns it. Both teams block each other's changes, approval processes become unclear, and cost attribution is impossible.
:::

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: No workspace decommissioning process.** Workspaces left running after a project ends cost money and represent unmonitored attack surface. Every workspace must have an owner and a review date.
:::

### Self-Assessment — Pillar 4

| Capability | Level 1 | Level 3 | Level 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Naming convention | No convention | Documented but inconsistently followed | Enforced via OPA policy on workspace create |
| RBAC | Shared admin access | Role-based per project | Workspace-scoped RBAC with least-privilege service accounts |
| Workspace provisioning | Manual UI creation | Documented process | Self-service via IaCM pipeline or catalog |
| Lifecycle management | No process | Ad-hoc decommissioning | Automated quarterly reviews with cost-based alerting |
| Tagging | No workspace tags | Some tags | Mandatory tags enforced, untagged workspaces auto-flagged |

## Pillar 5: Cost & FinOps Integration

> *"The cheapest infrastructure is the infrastructure you didn't provision by accident. The second cheapest is the infrastructure you right-sized before it went live."*

### Design Principles

1. **Cost is a pre-apply gate, not a post-billing surprise.** Engineers see the monthly cost delta of their Terraform change before they click apply — every single time.
2. **IaC changes are tagged for cost attribution.** Every resource created by a Terraform pipeline carries tags that map to a team, application, environment, and cost centre in your FinOps tool.
3. **Budgets are connected to workspaces.** Each workspace has an associated budget in Harness CCM. When a pipeline apply would breach the budget, the approval gate highlights the variance.
4. **Infrastructure is provisioned with a TTL where appropriate.** Ephemeral environments (dev, test, demo) use AutoStopping or scheduled destroy pipelines. They are not left running 24/7.
5. **Right-sizing is continuous.** Harness CCM recommendations are reviewed as part of the platform engineering sprint cycle and linked back to IaC changes.
6. **Cost anomalies trigger IaC investigation.** When CCM detects a cost spike, the first investigation step is checking which IaCM pipeline ran near that time.

### Cost Estimation in the Pipeline

```
terraform plan output
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────────┐      ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│   Infracost CLI   │─────►│  Cost Report                    │
│   (Plugin step)   │      │  ─────────────────────────────  │
└───────────────────┘      │  Monthly cost (before): $1,240  │
                           │  Monthly cost (after):  $3,890  │
                           │  Delta:                +$2,650  │
                           │                                  │
                           │  Top cost drivers:               │
                           │  • aws_instance.app  +$1,800/mo  │
                           │  • aws_rds_cluster   +$850/mo    │
                           └─────────────────────────────────┘
                                        │
                                        ▼
                             ┌─────────────────┐
                             │  Budget Gate    │
                             │  > $5k → block  │
                             │  > $1k → warn   │
                             └─────────────────┘
```

### Cost Tagging Strategy

Every resource provisioned via IaCM must carry these tags:

| Tag Key | Example Value | FinOps Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Environment` | `production` | Filter prod vs non-prod |
| `Team` | `platform-engineering` | Team-level chargeback |
| `Application` | `payments-service` | Per-application cost |
| `CostCentre` | `CC-4712` | Finance chargeback code |
| `Owner` | `sam.smith@company.com` | Accountability |
| `ManagedBy` | `harness-iacm` | Identify IaCM resources |
| `Workspace` | `tuk-platform-payments-prod-use1` | Workspace-level tracking |
| `TerraformVersion` | `1.8.0` | Version tracking |

**Enforce via OPA policy:**
```rego
package terraform.cost_tags

required := {"Environment","Team","Application","CostCentre","Owner","ManagedBy"}

deny[msg] {
  resource := input.resource_changes[_]
  resource.change.after != null
  missing := required - {k | resource.change.after.tags[k]}
  count(missing) > 0
  msg := sprintf("'%v' missing cost allocation tags: %v", [resource.address, missing])
}
```

### TTL / AutoStopping for Ephemeral Environments

| Environment Type | Expected Lifetime | Recommended Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Feature branch dev | Hours to days | Harness AutoStopping rule + destroy pipeline on PR close |
| Sprint testing | Days to weeks | Scheduled destroy pipeline (cron, business hours only) |
| Demo / sandbox | Days | AutoStopping with idle detection |
| Integration testing | Pipeline duration | Destroy stage at end of CI pipeline |
| Staging | Permanent | AutoStopping on out-of-hours (20:00–06:00) |
| Production | Permanent | Right-sizing recommendations via CCM |

### CCM ↔ IaCM Integration Loop

```
Harness CCM (FinOps)
        │
        ├─► Cost Anomaly Detected
        │     └─► Investigate: which IaCM pipeline ran at T-1h?
        │
        ├─► Recommendation: Downsize instance
        │     └─► Create IaC PR → pipeline apply → cost reduction
        │
        ├─► Budget Alert: 85% consumed
        │     └─► Notify workspace owner → review pending applies
        │
        └─► Cost Attribution: Tag-based
              └─► Workspace tags propagate to CCM perspectives
                  └─► Cost breakdown by team/app/environment
```

### Anti-Patterns

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: No cost estimation before apply.** Engineers applying `terraform apply` without seeing the cost delta is the infrastructure equivalent of shopping without looking at prices. Infracost takes < 30 seconds to run and prevents surprise cloud bills.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Dev environments running 24/7.** Unmanaged development environments typically waste 60–70% of their cost running idle overnight and on weekends. Implement AutoStopping or scheduled destroy/apply pipelines for all non-production environments.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: All resources tagged `Environment: production`.** When every resource is tagged production (to avoid AutoStopping), FinOps loses visibility and cost allocation becomes meaningless. Enforce correct environment tagging via OPA.
:::

### Self-Assessment — Pillar 5

| Capability | Level 1 | Level 3 | Level 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cost estimation | No estimation | Manual Infracost run | Infracost in every apply pipeline with budget gate |
| Cost tagging | No tags or inconsistent | Partial tagging | OPA-enforced mandatory tags on all resources |
| Ephemeral environments | Always-on | Manual teardown | AutoStopping + scheduled destroy pipelines |
| Budget integration | No budgets | CCM budgets exist | Budget alerts linked to workspace apply gates |
| CCM ↔ IaCM feedback | Manual | Monthly review | Automated: anomaly → IaCM investigation → PR |

## Pillar 6: Developer Experience & Enablement

> *"The best governance is governance that developers don't have to think about — it's built into the platform, invisible when things are right, and clearly instructive when they're not."*

### Design Principles

1. **Self-service workspace onboarding.** A developer should be able to request a new IaCM workspace via a catalog form and have it fully provisioned (workspace, RBAC, backend, pipeline, monitoring) within minutes — with no platform engineering intervention.
2. **Golden path templates.** Provide opinionated, pre-approved pipeline and Terraform module templates that embed all security, compliance, and cost controls. Teams use the golden path by default and diverge only when necessary.
3. **Fast feedback loops.** A developer running a plan should see security findings, cost estimates, and policy violations in the same Harness UI — not across five different tool dashboards.
4. **Failure is instructive.** When a pipeline fails a policy check, the error message tells the developer exactly what to fix and why — not just `policy violation`.
5. **Onboarding is automated.** New team members get the right RBAC, workspace access, and runbook documentation automatically via provisioning pipeline.
6. **IaCM adoption is measured.** Track workspace count, pipeline frequency, scan coverage, drift rate, and cost attribution accuracy as platform KPIs. Review monthly.

### The Golden Path

```
Developer Experience                Platform Engineering Provides
──────────────────────              ─────────────────────────────

1. Request workspace                Catalog form → provisioning pipeline
   (Service Catalog form)           Creates: workspace, RBAC, backend,
                                    pipeline, monitoring, tags

2. Write Terraform code             Golden path module library
   (using approved modules)         Pre-vetted modules: VPC, EKS, RDS,
                                    GKE, Cloud SQL, Storage

3. Open Pull Request                Harness Code / GitHub integration
   (triggers plan pipeline)         Runs: plan → scan → cost estimate
                                    Posts results as PR comment

4. Review plan + scan results       Harness Pipeline UI
   (in Harness UI or PR)            Shows: plan diff, Wiz findings,
                                    cost delta, policy violations

5. Merge PR → pipeline apply        GitOps trigger
   (auto or manual trigger)         Runs: full lifecycle pipeline
                                    Approval gate with plan diff

6. Monitor workspace               Harness CCM + Drift pipeline
   (drift, cost, anomalies)         Alerts on drift, budget, anomalies
```

### Platform KPIs

::: metrics
- label: Workspace Coverage
  value: "Target: 100%"
  sub: resources managed by IaCM
- label: Scan Coverage
  value: "Target: 100%"
  sub: pipelines with security scan
- label: Drift Rate
  value: "Target: < 5%"
  sub: workspaces with active drift
- label: MTTR (Drift)
  value: "Target: < 4h"
  sub: time to remediate detected drift
- label: Cost Attribution
  value: "Target: > 95%"
  sub: resources with all required tags
- label: Self-Service %
  value: "Target: > 80%"
  sub: workspaces provisioned without platform ticket
:::

### Terraform Module Library

A curated library of approved, security-hardened Terraform modules is the foundation of developer enablement. Teams use pre-vetted modules rather than writing raw resource blocks.

**Module governance:**

| Module Tier | Security Review | OPA Compliant | Cost Estimated | Maintained By |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1 — Gold** | ✅ Full | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | Platform Engineering |
| **Tier 2 — Silver** | ✅ Basic | ✅ Yes | ⚠️ Partial | Team + Platform review |
| **Tier 3 — Bronze** | ⚠️ Self-attested | ⚠️ Partial | ❌ No | Team-owned |
| **Unvetted** | ❌ None | ❌ No | ❌ No | **Blocked by policy** |

**Recommended Tier 1 module catalogue:**

| Module | Provider | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| `tf-aws-vpc` | AWS | VPC, subnets, NAT, IGW, flow logs |
| `tf-aws-eks` | AWS | EKS cluster, node groups, IRSA |
| `tf-aws-rds-postgres` | AWS | RDS Aurora, parameter groups, encryption |
| `tf-aws-s3-secure` | AWS | S3 with encryption, versioning, public-access-block |
| `tf-gcp-gke` | GCP | GKE cluster, node pools, workload identity |
| `tf-gcp-cloudsql` | GCP | Cloud SQL, encryption, private IP |
| `tf-azure-aks` | Azure | AKS, managed identity, monitoring |

### Harness IDP Integration

Integrate with Harness Internal Developer Portal (IDP) for full self-service:

```
Harness IDP Service Catalog
         │
         ├─► Software Template: "Create IaCM Workspace"
         │     Input: team, app, environment, cloud, region
         │     Action: triggers provisioning pipeline
         │     Output: workspace URL, pipeline URL, runbook link
         │
         ├─► Scorecard: "IaCM Best Practices"
         │     Checks: security scan, drift detection, tagging, approval gates
         │     Score: 0-100, visible on every component page
         │
         └─► TechDocs: "IaCM Runbooks"
               Platform docs, migration guides, module docs
               Auto-synced from Git
```

### Anti-Patterns

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Platform engineering as a gatekeeper.** If every new workspace requires a Jira ticket, 5-day SLA, and platform engineer review, developers will bypass the process. Self-service is not a nice-to-have — it is a security requirement. Unsanctioned tools emerge when the sanctioned tool is too slow.
:::

:::warning
**Anti-pattern: Documentation that lives outside the platform.** Confluence pages get stale. Runbooks in TechDocs (co-located with code, auto-tested) stay current. Platform documentation should be as close to the code as possible.
:::

:::critical
**Anti-pattern: Treating IaCM adoption as a one-time project.** IaCM is a capability, not a migration. Adoption rates, drift rates, scan coverage, and cost attribution accuracy must be measured continuously and reviewed in the platform engineering sprint.
:::

### Self-Assessment — Pillar 6

| Capability | Level 1 | Level 3 | Level 5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workspace provisioning | Manual + ticket | Documented process, <5 day SLA | Self-service catalog, <15 min automated provisioning |
| Module library | No shared modules | Shared modules in Git | Tiered governance model, Tier 1 gold modules enforced |
| Developer feedback | Pipeline logs only | Scan results in Harness UI | PR comments with plan, cost, scan, policy in one view |
| Platform KPIs | Not measured | Quarterly review | Monthly dashboard, automated alerts on regression |
| IDP integration | None | Basic catalog | Full scorecard, templates, TechDocs |

Use this scorecard to assess your overall IaCM Well-Architected posture.

| Pillar | Weight | Your Score (1–5) | Weighted Score |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline Design & Lifecycle | 20% | ___ | ___ |
| Security & Compliance | 25% | ___ | ___ |

| Cost & FinOps Integration | 10% | ___ | ___ |
| Developer Experience | 10% | ___ | ___ |

### Maturity Bands

| Score | Band | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 – 1.9 | **Foundational** | IaCM module enabled, some pipelines exist, manual processes dominate |
| 2.0 – 2.9 | **Developing** | Core lifecycle pipelines running, basic approval gates, some templating |
| 3.0 – 3.9 | **Defined** | Consistent pipeline patterns, security scanning, drift detection, tagging |
| 4.0 – 4.5 | **Managed** | OPA policies, cost estimation, self-service, measured KPIs |
| 4.6 – 5.0 | **Optimised** | Auto-remediation, FinOps feedback loop, SBOM, full self-service |

## Prioritised Improvement Roadmap

### Phase 1 — Harden the Foundation (0–30 days)

:::action
**1. Security scan coverage: 100%.** Apply the existing `account.TU_SEAL_IAC_Scan_Templates` Wiz scan template to all pipelines that currently lack it. This is a 2-hour effort with zero new tooling.
:::

:::action
**2. Approval gates on all destructive operations.** Add `IACMApproval` with `autoApprove: false` and `timeout: 24h` to every destroy pipeline. No exceptions.
:::

:::action
**3. Mandatory tags via OPA.** Create an account-level OPA policy enforcing `Environment`, `Team`, `Owner`, and `CostCentre` on all resources. Block on non-compliance.
:::

:::action
**4. Drift detection on all production workspaces.** Create a scheduled drift pipeline (daily, 08:00 UTC) for every production workspace. Alert on Slack/PagerDuty when drift is detected.
:::

### Phase 2 — Add Governance (30–90 days)

:::action
**5. Infracost in the scan template.** Add Infracost as a Plugin step to `account.TU_SEAL_IAC_Scan_Templates`. All 13 template-referencing pipelines get cost estimation automatically. Set a $5k/month gate.
:::

:::action
**6. Org-level templates for all 5 orgs.** TU UK already has `org.pipeline_terraform_apply`. Create equivalent org templates for TU Africa, OneTru, International Markets, and Global Infrastructure.
:::

:::action
**7. OIDC credentials.** Replace long-lived AWS access keys with OIDC role assumption on all AWS connectors. Replace GCP service account keys with Workload Identity Federation.
:::

:::action
**8. Harness STO adoption.** Migrate all standalone Wiz shell-script integrations to native Harness STO stages. This provides centralised findings dashboard, historical trending, and severity-gated promotion.
:::

### Phase 3 — Optimise & Scale (90–180 days)

:::action
**9. Self-service workspace provisioning.** Build a Harness IDP Service Catalog template that provisions IaCM workspaces end-to-end: workspace creation, RBAC assignment, pipeline creation, monitoring setup. Target SLA: < 15 minutes.
:::

:::action
**10. Tier 1 module library.** Establish a Platform Engineering-maintained set of gold modules for the top 10 infrastructure patterns (VPC, EKS/GKE, RDS, S3, etc.). Enforce via OPA that all new resources use Tier 1 or Tier 2 modules.
:::

:::action
**11. CCM ↔ IaCM feedback loop.** Connect Harness CCM cost anomalies to IaCM pipeline run history. When a cost spike is detected, automatically surface which IaCM pipeline ran nearest to the spike time.
:::

:::action
**12. Automated drift remediation.** Extend drift detection pipelines to not just alert, but create a Jira ticket with the drift diff and optionally trigger a remediation apply pipeline — with approval gate — when drift is detected on production workspaces.
:::

## Appendix A: Real-World Patterns Reference

The following patterns were observed in live production pipelines analysed during framework development.

| Pattern | Observed In | Adoption Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Unified lifecycle pipeline (TF_Action variable) | TU Africa / AISADMINIAC | Recommended for all new workspaces |
| Org-level pipeline template | TU UK | Mandatory for all orgs |
| Vault AppRole dynamic credentials | OneTru / Vanguard | Recommended where Vault is available |
| Dynamic workspace naming from env variables | OneTru / Vanguard | Best practice for multi-env deployments |
| Account-level security scan template | TU Africa / TU UK | Mandatory — centralise all security controls |
| Dedicated drift pipeline (schedulable) | TU UK | Recommended alongside embedded drift step |
| CloudFormation → Terraform migration pipeline | TU Africa | Reference pattern for all legacy migrations |
| State file migration pipeline | TU Africa | Mandatory — no manual state ops |

| `IACMTerraformPlugin` | `apply` | Apply the plan, provision resources |
